The US FDA has launched a Rare Disease Framework Initiative that is designed to reflect "the realities of rare disease drug development by considering the nuances of each disease, patient needs, product type and the evidence that can be realistically generated in small patient populations."
A white paper on the program states that there is a significant unmet need for rare diseases given that only 5% of such ailments have an FDA-approved treatment.

"While flexibility is built into the regulatory framework for drug development and approval of therapies addressing unmet medical need, the FDA needs to leverage recent technologies and scientific understanding of the biologic basis for any particular rare disease coupled with the perspectives of the patient to maximize the use of current authorities that can ensure scientific rigor without unnecessary demands that are infeasible for diseases that affect small patient populations," according to the document.
The agency is asking for feedback from patients and disease advocates and will hold an Oct. 28 meeting.

title: FDA unveils rare disease initiative to enhance therapy development
